title: How to Build Trustworthy AI — Allie Howe
talk_summary: A GRC/security consultant's overview of 'trustworthy AI' framed as AI security (external attacks on your app) plus AI safety (your app harming the world), delivered through MLSecOps, red teaming, and runtime guardrails.

takeaways.technique: Runtime input/output guardrail layer near the model
takeaways.what_they_do: Insert a validation step on both the prompt going into the model and the response coming out, blocking off-topic, unsafe, or policy-violating content before it reaches the user or downstream service.

takeaways.technique: Custom guardrails encoding business-specific forbidden actions
takeaways.what_they_do: Beyond generic PII/toxicity filters, define app-specific rules like 'never modify patient records' or 'never recommend a competitor', enforced at runtime by keyword/topic restriction.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I have configured my guardrails to restrict this topic and this key and keywords related to this so that we can make sure to not change um patient data

takeaways.technique: Cross-model comparison as a cheap backdoor/behavior probe
takeaways.what_they_do: Send the same prompt to multiple models and flag large response divergence as a signal that one model is misbehaving or backdoored.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you ask every single model the same question, but one had a really different response, you might be like, okay, maybe this model like one either doesn't work appropriately

takeaways.technique: Red-team suite that feeds runtime guardrail config
takeaways.what_they_do: Continuously test the app with adversarial and safety prompts, then use the failures to decide which topics/prompts to block at runtime.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can use them to influence a runtime guardrail ... we can block certain um topics and prompts that would elicit those responses

takeaways.technique: Scan downloaded model artifacts for unsafe deserialization
takeaways.what_they_do: Run a scanner (ModelScan) over models pulled from hubs/zoos to detect embedded code that executes on load (pickle unsafe operators).
takeaways.evidence_quote: you're getting these models say from a model repository or a model zoo on the web and you're just downloading it. You need to scan those
